findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh the connected calendars query, so the cache status stays stale
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the parent's onSuccess callback. It never invalidates `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, which is the query that supplies `cacheUpdatedAt`. Unless the parent happens to refetch, the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Last updated' timestamp after the cache is deleted. The disconnect mutation does invalidate that query in onSettled, so the two flows are inconsistent.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US locale instead of the user's locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the locale already available from `useLocale()`. Users with other locales see English-formatted dates, which is inconsistent with the rest of the translated UI.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId with empty data is used as a write on every cache refresh
findings.body: CalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {})` on every cache refresh. Because SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is `@updatedAt`, this issues an UPDATE over every selected calendar of the credential, including event-type-scoped rows, just to bump a timestamp. The PR notes say this field is not displayed in the frontend and may be unnecessary. It adds write load to the hot refresh path and to unwatch flows without a clear consumer.

findings.title: Unconditional SelectedCalendar bulk update added to cache refresh path
findings.body: The new `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` runs after every cache population, including the remaining-calendars refresh in unwatchCalendar. It writes to every SelectedCalendar row for the credential even though the value is not used by any consumer in this PR. If it stays, it should at least be justified, or it should be scoped to the rows that actually changed.

findings.title: updatedAt relies on Prisma @updatedAt, which raw SQL writes will not touch
findings.body: CalendarCache.updatedAt is declared with `@default(now()) @updatedAt`, so it is only maintained by Prisma client writes. Any raw SQL or bulk update path will leave it stale, and the UI status would then be wrong. The comment mentions 'future raw inserts' but does not address raw updates.

findings.title: Migration header warning contradicts the SQL that follows
findings.body: The header says adding a required column without a default is not possible on a non-empty table, and the SQL then adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`. The header describes a situation the migration avoids, which is misleading for future maintainers. It should be updated or removed.

findings.title: No tests cover the new deleteCache handler or the cache status repository method
findings.body: The authorization check (credential must belong to user) and the cache deletion are untested, as is the new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groupBy and the enrichment in connectedCalendarsHandler. The PR's own checklist relies on manual E2E testing, which is not a substitute for regression tests on an access-control path.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId
findings.body: The Pick types for allSelectedCalendars and userLevelSelectedCalendars gained two required fields. Any existing caller that builds a UserWithCalendars object without those fields, including platform-libraries consumers of this exported type, will fail type-checking. This is a silent contract change unrelated to the feature.

findings.title: Session user query now exposes googleChannelId to the session payload
findings.body: findUnlockedUserForSession is used to build the session. The change adds googleChannelId (and updatedAt) to the selected calendars. This value is a Google push-channel identifier that is not needed for the session and should not be broadly serialized. The change is unrelated to the cache feature and widens the data exposed through the session.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx, but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. tsx is not listed in apps/web devDependencies, so `npx` will fetch it at runtime, which is non-deterministic and depends on network and registry state. The change is also unrelated to the calendar cache feature and is not mentioned in the title. It should be a separate PR, with tsx added as a pinned devDependency if it is needed.

findings.title: Rate-limit path exits with status 0 and sed -i is not portable
findings.body: cleanup() always ends with `exit 0`, so the rate-limit branch and the 'Failed to extract URL' branch both report success to the caller. Also, `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU/Linux, where the script would error when updating ENV_FILE. The script also writes to ../.env relative to the CWD. The script is unrelated to the feature and is undocumented.
